_meta.indication: For adults and pediatric patients (12 years of age and older and weighing at least 40 kg) for the treatment of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) requiring hospitalization.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-national, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; RDV 200 mg on Day 1 then 100 mg on Days 2-10 IV vs placebo, randomized 1:1
pivotal_trials.population: Hospitalized patients with mild, moderate, or severe COVID-19 with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to recovery through Day 29 (recovery = ordinal category 1, 2, or 3 on an 8-point scale)
pivotal_trials.result: Median time to recovery 10 days RDV vs 15 days placebo; hazard ratio 1.29 (95% CI 1.12 to 1.49). Key secondary odds of improvement at Day 15 OR 1.54 (95% CI 1.25 to 1.91). 29-day mortality 11% RDV vs 15% placebo (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.03), not statistically significant.

key_safety: Major safety issues were hepatotoxicity (transaminase elevations) and hypersensitivity reactions (including infusion-related and anaphylactic reactions). The most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5%) were nausea, ALT increased, and AST increased. Grade >=3 adverse reactions occurred in 8% of VEKLURY vs 9% of placebo subjects in ACTT-1.
target_moa: Remdesivir is a SARS-CoV-2 nucleotide analog RNA polymerase inhibitor; a direct-acting antiviral that inhibits viral RNA synthesis.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected.

description.text: Added a 3-day dosing regimen for treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in non-hospitalized adults and pediatric patients (≥12 years, ≥40 kg) at high risk for progression to severe disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the use of Veklury (remdesivir) as a 3-day dosing regimen for the treatment of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in adults and pediatric patients (12 years of age and older and weighing at least 40 kg) with positive results of direct severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) viral testing, who are not hospitalized and have mild-to-moderate COVID-19, and are at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19, including hospitalization or death.

basis.text: Fast Track designation was granted in March 2020 for IND 147753 (COVID-19).

citations.quote: Milestone regulatory events for IND 147753 included the granting of Fast Track designation in March 2020, Rolling Review in April 2020, and Emergency Use Authorization in May 2020.

summary.text: Remdesivir was developed under IND 147753 for COVID-19 (opened February 2020), receiving Fast Track designation in March 2020, Rolling Review in April 2020, and Emergency Use Authorization in May 2020; the NDA received August 7, 2020 was approved without accelerated approval as the first FDA-approved drug for COVID-19, with the application not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: In February 2020, IND 147753 for the treatment of COVID-19 was opened.
Milestone regulatory events for IND 147753 included the granting of Fast Track designation in March 2020, Rolling Review in April 2020, and Emergency Use Authorization in May 2020.
RDV, a direct acting antiviral drug that inhibits viral RNA synthesis, would be the first drug approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of COVID-19.
